title: Serotonin-reuptake inhibitors act centrally to cause bone loss in mice by counteracting a local anti-resorptive effect
authors: Ortuño MJ, Robinson ST, Subramanyam P, Paone R, Huang YY, Guo XE, et al.
population: Wild-type female mice treated with fluoxetine at plasma concentrations similar to human therapeutic levels for 3 or 6 weeks; osteoclast cultures
funder: The National Institute of Health grant AG032959 (PD) supported this work.
authorConflicts: Authors declare no competing financial interest.
result: In mice, 3 weeks of fluoxetine raised bone volume through a direct, serotonin reuptake-independent inhibition of osteoclast differentiation (Ca2+-calmodulin-NFATc1), whereas 6 weeks caused net bone loss with lower bone formation, through a brain serotonin-dependent rise in sympathetic output; co-treatment with propranolol prevented the bone loss. Animal data.
